clue.text: Hit the bottle? Moi? In a Greek temple?

parts.note: the French for 'me', as Miss Piggy says it
to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone accused of drinking protests their innocence, asking whether such a thing could happen in a Greek temple.
explanation.walkthrough: ME TOPE reads as 'I drink'; the order is Moi then the drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A metope is the square panel between triglyphs on the frieze of a Doric temple, found in Greek architecture.

clue.text: Beckham's previous complaint about glitch that lost cup

indicators.note: the complaint word goes round, surrounding what follows

parts.note: a moan is a grumble

indicators.note: the glitch word must shed a part, the part named straight after these words

parts.note: a hiccup is a minor setback
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer grumbles about the mishap that cost his team the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' looks like a football trophy, but it is the tail of the glitch word. David Beckham famously wore a Mohican haircut, a ridge of hair over a shaved head, before moving on to other styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckham's earlier hairstyle was the Mohican, a strip of hair down the middle of an otherwise shaved head.

clue.text: A bone, roughly, in the main body

parts.note: a T-bone is named after its T-shaped bone, so the letter T stands for the bone
'or so' means approximately

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson places a particular bone somewhere around the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The bone is a T, as in a T-bone steak; adding 'or so' makes it a T, roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the trunk of the human body, the main part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Accompaniment to cheque isn't sincere when service follows

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the statement that comes with wages
second meaning: split in two it is the start of a phrase for insincere support, completed by the word service

explanation.surface: A pay cheque arrives with a note, and the gesture is hollow if a church service comes after.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PAYS LIP, then add 'service': to pay lip service is to express support without meaning it.
explanation.definitionFit: A payslip is the itemised statement handed to an employee along with their wages, often with the cheque.

clue.text: 9 or fish from New York?
The rude military?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., not civilian

explanation.surface: A complaint that soldiers are a bad-mannered bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke reading: the military are the opposite of civilians, so they are 'un-civil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncivil means discourteous and impolite, and split up jokingly it means not of the civilian population.

clue.text: Church job appertaining to the Senior Service?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the office of an elder in a Presbyterian church
second meaning: split jokingly, a vessel belonging to the senior arm of the forces

explanation.surface: A church post somehow connected with the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Senior Service is the Royal Navy, Britain's oldest armed service; read as ELDER SHIP, the word becomes a senior vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldership is the position held by a church elder, a lay office in Presbyterian and similar congregations.

clue.text: Needlework's more liberal

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies its letter
ample means generous, so ampler is more generous

explanation.surface: A claim that sewing is a more permissive pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Needlework's does double duty: it leaves the definition and joins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is an embroidered panel showing a range of stitches, a classic piece of needlework.

clue.text: No more Methodist ministers allowed on TV?

definitions.text: No more Methodist ministers allowed on TV?

parts.words: No more Methodist ministers allowed on TV?
parts.note: surface reading: a ban on preachers appearing in broadcasts
setter's reading: a Methodist group of churches sharing ministers that admits no newcomers, and also a kind of private television system

explanation.surface: A broadcaster bans Methodist clergy from appearing on television.
explanation.walkthrough: In Methodism a circuit is a group of churches served by a team of ministers; one admitting no more is shut. Closed-circuit TV is a private camera network.
explanation.definitionFit: Closed-circuit television is a private camera system, and the phrase also describes a shut Methodist ministry district.

clue.text: Brave man and layabout among volunteers to join rebel: my 22 has no support

indicators.note: the brave man and the shuffled word sit inside the volunteers

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: 'layabout' ends in about, which says the letters before it are turned around in a new order

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
the first three letters, with the rest of the word acting as the shuffle signal
Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recruitment story about a hero and an idler signing up with a rebel, ending with something collapsing for want of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is RAPIER; with no PIER (support) it leaves RA, the abbreviation for the Royal Academy. HERO plus YAL go inside TA.
explanation.definitionFit: RA is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Academy, the London institution of artists, obtained here from RAPIER minus a supporting pier.

clue.text: See 4
Trust Ballesteros as to how he may be handicapped?

definitions.text: as to how he may be handicapped?

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golfer
to trust is to rely on

explanation.surface: Backing a golfer to perform well despite his handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer; golf handicaps make 'handicapped' look like sport rather than an adverb clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely describes the degree to which someone is badly handicapped, answering how he may be handicapped.

clue.text: Revolutionary painter without a bit of personality must be brave

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns order, so the painter's letters are turned upside down
the painter must go without the article that follows, losing it

parts.note: taken as written
the letter removed from the painter
in Freud the id is one part of the psyche

explanation.surface: An artist who joins a revolution needs courage even if he lacks charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: PAINTER without A leaves PINTER, which is rearranged; the id is the instinctive part of the personality in Freud's model.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold, a close synonym for brave in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Netted 100 lire at Rugby Union dance

indicators.note: dancers move about, so the listed letters move into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written
taken as written
the standard abbreviation of the sport

explanation.surface: Someone pocketed a hundred lire at a rugby club dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Netted' looks like 'won' or 'pocketed', but it is the definition: like a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticular means having the form of a network, so something reticular resembles a mesh of netting.

clue.text: City dwelling between second and sixth in scale

indicators.note: the dwelling sits between the two notes, so they enclose it

parts.note: in sol-fa the notes run do, re, mi, fa, so, la, so the sixth is la
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A musical joke about living somewhere in the middle of the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The scale is the sol-fa scale of singing; 'between' does not fix which note comes first, and here the sixth leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of the province of Punjab.

clue.text: Costermonger's duck

indicators.note: a monger deals and trades, so the word before it is dealt out again in a fresh order

parts.note: the first six letters, with the rest of the word acting as the shuffle signal

explanation.surface: A street trader's duck, perhaps a bird for sale on a barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a London street seller; the word splits so that its first half is the fodder and its second half the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts, a member of the diving duck family.

clue.text: See 8
Language of love?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Latin-derived language such as French or Spanish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Language of love' is a stock phrase for French; here the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance is the family of languages descended from Latin, and also a love affair or loving feeling.

clue.text: Work hard during stop to find bookmark

indicators.note: the hard work happens during the stop, so it is held inside it

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
op is short for opus, a work
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone toils during a break in order to locate a lost bookmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmark' is read as a book's mark, a printer's emblem, not something kept between pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A colophon is a publisher's emblem or inscription printed in a volume, literally a mark in a book.

clue.text: A crazy fellow in church, he gave a sermon on the beach

definitions.text: he gave a sermon on the beach

indicators.note: the crazy fellow is placed inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written
a nut is a madman

explanation.surface: A mad preacher who holds services on the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: King Canute (Cnut) sat on the shore and failed to command the tide, a lesson to flattering courtiers that his power had limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend has King Canute on the beach showing his courtiers that the waves would not obey him, a moral lesson.

clue.text: Ring writer to get fat and emperor when love's lost

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: the emperor has something lost, so one letter is taken away from him

parts.note: the Roman emperor Nero
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Advice to a writer: put on weight and become an emperor once romance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like Wagner's operas, but it is the first name of Ring Lardner, the American sports writer and humorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring Lardner was an American short-story writer and sports journalist, so he is a writer named Ring.

clue.text: Supervise poems written in Old English

indicators.note: the poems are set down inside the language that follows

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: An instruction to edit a collection of Anglo-Saxon poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work, the same as to supervise it.

clue.text: Lorry driver on traffic island

parts.note: truck is dealings, as in 'have no truck with'
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A trucker stranded on a traffic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic island' reads as a road feature, but traffic is a separate word for trade, and the island is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A truckman is someone who drives a truck, the American word for a lorry, so a lorry driver.

clue.text: Just the thing for … for a piercing blow

parts.note: the letters run across the ends and start of these words
surface padding that completes the picture of a thrust

explanation.surface: Something ideal, says the clue, for delivering a sharp stab.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leaves the definition open-ended; the answer sits in plain sight across three words, with no separate signal beyond the whole clue's hint of a piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, the ideal weapon for delivering a piercing stab.

clue.text: Indian city on a river? On the contrary

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
taken as written
taken as written
an instruction to put the pieces in the opposite order to the clue's

explanation.surface: Is this Indian city on a river? No, the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' swaps the order of the pieces: not 'on a' then river, but river then 'on a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona, now Pune, is a large city in Maharashtra, western India.

clue.text: Sticker left with nothing else on river home of 9

parts.note: a bur is a seed head that sticks to clothing

indicators.note: else means otherwise, so the word before it is taken in another order

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written
the Ouse, one of several English rivers of that name

explanation.surface: A burr left with nothing else stranded on a river, its home.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is the Royal Academy, whose London home is Burlington House on Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlington House on Piccadilly houses the Royal Academy of Arts, making it the residence of the clue at 9.

clue.text: Country bird that flopped

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nation spanning Europe and Asia

explanation.walkthrough: 'that flopped' is a third meaning: a turkey is also a show or film that fails badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a nation straddling Europe and Asia, a large farmyard fowl, and slang for a theatrical failure.

clue.text: Amusing place, as with part of 24, reminiscent of pastoral life?
